answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (compliance forbids reverting the security patch), so memory_b1 doesn't apply. Write-path p99 climbing during the daily settlement write peak points to capacity contention on the write path, making add_capacity the most direct fit — memory_b3 shows headroom absorbed a prior surge cleanly. Regional failover (memory_b2) is the fallback if latency is regional rather than capacity-bound, so I verify both before committing. Circuit breakers (b4) target a partner dependency outage, which isn't indicated here, and read-replica routing (b5) wouldn't relieve a write-path problem. Risk flagged: adding capacity mid-peak on a freshly patched release carries some interaction risk, so I'd stage it and watch write latency and error rates closely rather than assume the new build isn't the cause.
